p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing a conversed mechanism for oxidative decarboxylation. There are three columns of chains in this image. The first is pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, which begina with the pyruvate chain, where O double binds down to C, which binds left to CH3 and right to COO- (all in pink). A black arrow points down to the acetyl-CoA. In the middle of the arrow another black arrow points to the left to CO2. On the right side of the black arrow, HS-CoA and NAD+ each point to NADH (in an orange oval) with red arrows. The aceytl-CoA chain begins with C, which binds left to CH3, down and right to S-CoA, and double binds up and right to O. The second column is th citric acid cycle. It begins at the top with the alpha-ketoglutarate chain, where -OOC binds right to CH2, which binds rights CH2 (in pink box). CH2 binds right to C, which binds right to COO- and double binds up to O (all in pink box). A black arrow points down to the succinyl-CoA molecule. In the middle of the arrow is the same as in pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. The succinyl-CoA molecule bgins with -OOC bonds right to CH2, which bonds rights to CH2, which bonds right to C. C bonds down and right to S-CoA, and double bonds up and right to O. The final column is oxidation of isoleucine (leucine, valine) and begins with the alpha-keto acide from isoleucine molecule. It begins with CH3, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH (in pink box). CH bonds right to C (both in pink box) and up to CH3. C bonds right to COO- and double bonds up to O. A black arrow points down to the alpha-methylbutylryl-CoA molecule. The middle of the arrow is the same as the first two. The alpha-methylbutyryl-CoA molecule begins with CH3, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH. CH bonds up to CH3 and right to C, which bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA.
